samples.summary: The new path test only asserts `path.isAbsolute`, never the resolution BASE — a fix resolving against the wrong directory would pass
samples.evidence: scripts/agent/eval/score-all.test.mjs:706 asserts only `path.isAbsolute(value)` for `--root` and `--from` on every child argv. Nothing pins what those absolute paths resolve TO: had `scoreAll` used `path.resolve(agentDir, rootArg)` or `path.resolve(HERE, outArg)` (which is the very class of mistake the change is fixing), every child would still be handed an absolute path and this test's headline assertion would pass. The root case is partly rescued indirectly (the full pass completes, and the second test at :733 checks `path.join(parent, "no-such-store")`), but `--from` / `out` has no such check anywhere: no assertion compares any `--from` value to `path.join(parent, "payloads", ...)`. Adding one equality assertion would close it.

samples.summary: The `--from` half of the bug cannot actually fail in the test, because the spy child shares the driver's process and cwd
samples.evidence: fullPassSpy (score-all.test.mjs:632-638) reads the payload with `readFileSync(at("--from"))` inside the SAME process and cwd as the driver, so a relative `--from` resolves identically for both and the real failure mode (ENOENT on a file the driver had just written, described in score-all.mjs:568-572) is unreproducible here. The only thing standing between that regression and green is the `isAbsolute` proxy assertion at :706. The comment at :620-623 claims persist "actually WRITE[s] through the store … a test of the orchestration rather than of a mock", which overstates what the mock can detect: it never emulates a different cwd. A child spy that resolved `--from` against a different base (e.g. `path.resolve(otherDir, value)`) would make the coverage real.

samples.summary: The default `out` branch (`outDir = path.join(root, ".score-all")`) is exercised by no test
samples.evidence: score-all.mjs:579 and :605 add `out = outArg ? path.resolve(outArg) : null` and keep the `out ?? path.join(root, ".score-all")` default. The only full-pass test (score-all.test.mjs:655) always passes `out: "payloads"`; every other `scoreAll` test in the file (:559-593, :719) rejects before `outDir` is computed. So the null-`out` path — the one the CLI takes whenever `--out` is omitted — never runs in the suite, and a mistake there (e.g. resolving against cwd instead of root) would ship green. Low impact since `root` is now absolute, but it is untested behaviour on a changed line.

samples.summary: The refusal test's cleanup runs before the assertion it guards settles, so it depends on `scoreAll` throwing synchronously
samples.evidence: score-all.test.mjs:729 does `return assert.rejects(...)` inside a `try`, so the `finally` at :738 executes `process.chdir(cwd)` synchronously before the returned promise settles. It works today only because `scoreAll` reaches `refuse` with no intervening `await`, so `path.resolve` runs while cwd is still `parent`. If any await is ever introduced before the corpus check, the resolved path becomes cwd-dependent and this test breaks for a reason unrelated to the behaviour under test (it would go red, not silently pass). `await assert.rejects(...)` in an async test removes the coupling.
